findings.problem: Unsafe block with x86_64 std::arch intrinsics (_mm_add_ps, _mm_loadu_ps, _mm_storeu_ps, _mm_setzero_ps) without any explicit user waiver. Power of Ten strict mode and the Holzman Rust skill forbid unsafe by default; unsafe SIMD requires explicit user approval before code is written.
findings.failure_mode: Undefined behavior from unproven aliasing, uninitialized memory reads, or CPU-feature mismatch at runtime. Code ships unsafe intrinsics without documented preconditions, postconditions, or waiver trail.
findings.fix: Obtain explicit user waiver naming the waived rule before any unsafe SIMD. Rewrite using safe portable SIMD (std::simd with #![feature(portable_simd)] and #![forbid(unsafe_code)]) or a safe crate. If std::arch is required, wrap in a function annotated with #[target_feature] and guard with runtime CPU feature detection.

findings.problem: Hand-written unsafe SIMD using x86_64 target intrinsics. Safe SIMD (std::simd portable SIMD) or auto-vectorized scalar is the default. Unsafe target intrinsics in first-party code require explicit user approval and are a rejection trigger.
findings.failure_mode: Correctness cannot be verified by the compiler. The unsafe block is invisible to clippy -D unsafe_code, geiger, and standard static analysis without an explicit waiver record.
findings.fix: Replace with #![feature(portable_simd)] and std::simd types (Simd<f32, 4>). Keep #![forbid(unsafe_code)] on the crate. Use non-panicking load APIs (load_or_default, load_or) with length proofs.

findings.problem: No scalar reference implementation exists for comparison. The SIMD pattern requires a scalar correctness oracle, and SIMD without one is a rejection trigger.
findings.failure_mode: No way to verify the SIMD implementation produces the same numeric result as a correct scalar path. Float summation order differs between scalar (left-to-right) and SIMD (interleaved lanes), producing different results.
findings.fix: Add a scalar implementation (e.g. input.iter().copied().sum()) and property tests verifying SIMD output matches scalar for small, edge, and large inputs.

findings.problem: The loop processes 4 elements per iteration without remainder handling. When input.len() is not a multiple of 4, _mm_loadu_ps reads uninitialized memory past the end of the slice. chunks_exact is never used.
findings.failure_mode: Reads uninitialized heap memory on non-aligned inputs, producing garbage results. This is undefined behavior in unsafe code and a data-leak risk.
findings.fix: Use chunks_exact(4) to separate the aligned body from the remainder, process remainder with a scalar tail loop, and test empty, one, non-multiple, and large inputs.

findings.problem: The function is gated only by #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")] with no runtime CPU feature detection. _mm_setzero_ps, _mm_add_ps, _mm_loadu_ps, and _mm_storeu_ps are SSE1 intrinsics that require the CPU to support them. On QEMU, some VMs, or CPUs without SSE, this will trigger an illegal instruction at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal instruction crash at runtime on x86_64 platforms that lack SSE or where the OS cleared the SSE flag.
findings.fix: Add #[target_feature(enable = "sse")] to the function and guard calls with cfg!(target_feature = "sse") or use std::is_x86_feature_detected!("sse") for runtime dispatch. Provide a scalar fallback for non-SSE paths.

findings.problem: The unsafe block has no SAFETY comment documenting CPU feature provenance, bounds, alignment, aliasing, remainder handling, or drop safety. Unsafe invariant comments are required for any unsafe block after explicit waiver.
findings.failure_mode: Reviewers and future maintainers cannot verify the correctness of the unsafe code. No documented preconditions or postconditions.
findings.fix: Add a SAFETY: comment block stating CPU feature proof, bounds guarantee from chunks_exact, aliasing (input is read-only), remainder handling, and drop safety.

findings.problem: The while loop iterates while i < input.len() with no static upper bound. Power of Ten Rule 2 requires a fixed upper bound or mathematical termination proof for every loop. The iteration count depends entirely on input length at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: On untrusted or adversarial input, the loop has no bound. Combined with the missing remainder handling, this also risks out-of-bounds reads.
findings.fix: Replace with chunks_exact(4) which has a provable fixed iteration count. For Power of Ten strict mode, declare the maximum iteration count or use a while loop with a static cap (e.g., while i < input.len() && i < MAX_ITER * 4).

findings.problem: No rust-toolchain.toml exists. The crate uses edition 2021 with no toolchain pin. If this code is to use nightly features (portable_simd) or pass the zero-slippage gate, a checked-in rust-toolchain.toml with a pinned dated nightly is required.
findings.failure_mode: Floating toolchain can silently change compiler behavior, optimize differently, or remove features between nightly builds. CI and production builds may diverge.
findings.fix: Add rust-toolchain.toml with a pinned nightly channel (e.g., nightly-YYYY-MM-DD), profile minimal, and required components (rustfmt, clippy, rust-src, llvm-tools-preview).

findings.problem: No #![forbid(unsafe_code)] or #![deny(unsafe_code)] at crate level. The unsafe block compiles silently without any crate-level guard preventing future unsafe additions.
findings.failure_mode: Future code can add unsafe blocks without any compile-time objection. The crate has no unsafe-by-default policy enforced by the compiler.
findings.fix: Add #![forbid(unsafe_code)] to the crate root. Each unsafe block then requires an explicit #![allow(unsafe_code)] with a documented waiver.

findings.problem: The index arithmetic i += 4 uses unchecked addition. When input.len() is very large (near usize::MAX), this can wrap silently, producing an out-of-bounds pointer in _mm_loadu_ps(ptr). No checked or saturating arithmetic is used.
findings.failure_mode: Integer overflow on usize wraps to 0, causing the loop to re-read from the start of the buffer or compute a wildly incorrect pointer. In unsafe code, this is undefined behavior.
findings.fix: Use checked arithmetic (i = i.checked_add(4).unwrap()) or prefer chunks_exact which handles the stride internally with provable bounds.

findings.problem: The SIMD accumulation (MMX register-based f32 addition) uses a different summation order than scalar left-to-right f32 addition. IEEE 754 float addition is not associative; the SIMD result will differ from the scalar result even without NaN or overflow.
findings.failure_mode: Numeric results silently diverge from the scalar oracle. Downstream consumers comparing SIMD vs scalar outputs will see mismatches that are hard to diagnose.
findings.fix: Document the accepted numeric difference between SIMD and scalar. If bit-exact parity is required, use Kahan summation or pairwise reduction in both paths. If approximate results are acceptable, add property tests with tolerance.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists: no benchmark target, binary, or script in the crate. Without a benchmark, no performance claim can be made and the optimization cannot be validated.
no profiler evidence: no perf stat, cargo llvm-lines, or cargo bloat output to verify the SIMD path reduces cycles or instructions.
no second-ring evidence: no assembly (cargo asm) or LLVM IR (cargo llvm-ir) inspection to confirm the SIMD intrinsics are emitted and the scalar path is absent.
no tests: no test module, no unit tests, no property tests, and no scalar-vs-SIMD equivalence tests.
no rust-toolchain.toml: no pinned nightly toolchain for reproducible builds or nightly feature gating.
no release-provenance evidence: no cargo-semver-checks, cargo auditable, or SBOM for release artifact verification.
no safety verification: no Miri, Kani, or Crux run to verify the unsafe block against undefined behavior.
residual_risk: The crate contains a single unsafe SIMD function with no user waiver, no scalar oracle, no remainder handling, no runtime CPU feature detection, no tests, no benchmarks, no toolchain pin, and no crate-level unsafe guard. The unsafe block reads uninitialized memory on non-multiple-of-4 inputs and produces numerically different results from scalar float summation. All 10 Holzman Rust rules are violated. This crate must not ship until: (1) explicit unsafe waiver is obtained, (2) scalar oracle and property tests are added, (3) remainder handling is fixed, (4) runtime feature detection or target_feature guard is added, (5) #![forbid(unsafe_code)] is added to the crate root, (6) a rust-toolchain.toml is checked in, and (7) benchmark and profiler evidence proves the SIMD path wins.
